2.2.8 Variance and standard deviation of a random variable

If X is a random variable, then its variance is denoted by Var(X) or V(X) and its formula is given by

V(X)=E[X-E(X)]^2

\text{Or } V(X)=E[X^2]-[E(X)]^2

S.D(X)=\sqrt{V(X)}

Example 2.13

Consider the following discrete probability distribution:

Determine the mean, variance and standard deviation.

Solution:

\text{Mean}=E(X)=\Sigma x\,p(x)=7.2

\text{Variance}=V(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2=\Sigma x^2p(x)-[7.2]^2=56.6-51.84=4.76

\text{and}\quad S.D(X)=\sqrt{V(X)}=\sqrt{4.76}=2.181

2.2.9 Properties of variance and standard deviation of a random variable

Following are some of the important properties.

(i) The variance and standard deviation of a constant is equal to zero i.e. V(c)=0 and S.D(c)=0, where c is a constant.

Proof:

By definition V(X)=E[X-E(X)]^2

As the variable X is taking only a constant value c, therefore

V(c)=E[c-E(c)]^2

\phantom{V(c)}=E[c-c]^2\quad\because E(c)=c

\phantom{V(c)}=0

S.D(c)=\sqrt{0}=0

(ii) Variance and S.D of a random variable are not changed by adding/ subtracting a constant to/from the values of a random variable i.e.

$V(X\pm c)=V(X)$

Proof:

By definition V(X)=E[X-E(X)]^2

As (X+c) is a function of the random variable X, therefore,

V(X+c)=E[X+c-E(X+c)]^2

\phantom{V(X+c)}=E[X+c-E(X)-E(c)]^2

ثبوت:

تعریف کے مطابق V(X)=E[X-E(X)]^2

چونکہ متغیر X صرف ایک مستقل قیمت c لیتا ہے، اس لیے

V(c)=E[c-E(c)]^2

\phantom{V(c)}=E[c-c]^2\quad\because E(c)=c

\phantom{V(c)}=0

S.D(c)=\sqrt{0}=0

(ii) تصادفی متغیر کی قیمتوں میں کوئی مستقل جمع یا ان سے تفریق کرنے سے تصادفی متغیر کا تغیر اور معیاری انحراف تبدیل نہیں ہوتے، یعنی

$V(X\pm c)=V(X)$

ثبوت:

چونکہ (X+c) تصادفی متغیر X کا تفاعل ہے، اس لیے

V(X+c)=E[X+c-E(X+c)]^2

\phantom{V(X+c)}=E[X+c-E(X)-E(c)]^2
